config.placement_notes: Requested every layer on the GPU (launch.gpu_layers 999), 16 CPU threads, context 8192. Ollama imports the GGUF into its private store before the load. Observed placement is in the backend log and in fit/metadata.json of the attempt.

hardware_attestation.mux_hybrid_setting: MSHybrid (observed: Intel Graphics and NVIDIA both active display adapters, Intel drives internal 3840px panel; MSI Center GPU Switch not read directly)
hardware_attestation.gpu_tgp_power_limit: nvidia-smi power.limit N/A; default 95 W, max 175 W
hardware_attestation.model_ssd_filesystem: NTFS on the Windows C: NVMe volume (Phison 2TB NVMe ESR02TBTLCA3-E1J-2MS), read from the WSL guest through /mnt/c (9p). Ollama imports a copy into its private store on the ext4 virtual disk of the guest, on the same volume; LM Studio imports a symbolic link to the file, so it loads the file through /mnt/c.
hardware_attestation.carried_from_windows_attestation: bios, ram_configured_mhz, msi_power_fan_profile, mux_hybrid_setting and gpu_tgp_power_limit are the operator attestations of the native Windows runs of 2026-11-08 on the same machine; they were not read again for the WSL runs
hardware_attestation.wsl_memory_cap: guest MemTotal 51.0 GiB at the start of this run; swap 0 MiB (see wsl_config)
hardware_attestation.other_workloads: Hardware-fit measured runs on WSL2 Ubuntu 26.04 (guest of this Windows host): Ollama, then LM Studio, in one campaign. The model file is on the Windows NTFS volume and is read from the guest through /mnt/c; Ollama imports a copy into its private store on the guest disk, LM Studio imports a symbolic link to the file. The LM Studio desktop app (Linux AppImage) is open in the guest under WSLg, as its managed runs require. Notable Windows programs running at the start: consumer Ollama tray app, a Windows Ollama server, Microsoft Teams, VMware tray, VMware authorization service, ChatGPT desktop app, Claude desktop app, VS Code.
